name: Worgen
summary: Across Silverpine Forest, Ashenvale, and Duskwood, Worgen now hunt with bestial swiftness and a fury they cannot master. Once feared as nightmares from another realm, their beginnings remain uncertain.

sections.title: Whispers and Folktales
sections.body: Long before Worgen appeared in Lordaeron and Kalimdor, people told folktales and cautionary tales of wolf-men. Their beginnings remain a mystery. Scholars who have studied them believe they came to Azeroth from another realm. Archmage Arugal and the night elves' Scythe of Elune have both been shown to summon them.

sections.title: Arugal's Folly
sections.body:
During the Third War, the Scourge overran Lordaeron, and slain Kirin Tor wizards rose again as undead. Archmage Arugal sought a weapon to strengthen Dalaran's dwindling ranks. He used forbidden research by the Dalaran wizard Ur to pierce the veil and summon Worgen into Silverpine Forest. They savaged the undead invaders, but Arugal could not master their fury. The beasts turned on the wizards and spread their curse with fang and claw.

Mad with guilt and fascination, Arugal claimed the monsters as his children. He seized Baron Silverlaine's ancestral seat and renamed it Shadowfang Keep. There, he cursed nearby villagers into monstrous nocturnal servitude.

sections.title: The Scythe Awoken
sections.body:
Across the sea in Kalimdor, the night elf Sentinel Velinde Starsong sought to purge Felwood of the Burning Legion's lingering demonic remnants. She unearthed the Scythe of Elune and used the ancient relic to summon Worgen against the demonic satyrs.

As the battles raged, Velinde realized the scythe had slipped beyond her command. Worgen began appearing without her consent, slipping into Ashenvale's dark forests and beyond. Wild packs now roam, spreading terror wherever their moonlit hunts reach.

faq.answer: Worgen are fierce, upright lupine humanoids with terrifying strength, predatory senses, and dark shadow magic. They dwell mainly in secluded woodlands and ruins, hunting in packs under the pull of an uncontrollable bestial fury.

faq.q: Where did the worgen originally come from?
faq.answer: No one knows for certain where Worgen came from. They seem to come from another realm: Archmage Arugal summoned them into Silverpine from beyond, and the night elves' Scythe of Elune drew them forth in Kalimdor.

faq.q: How did worgen end up in Silverpine Forest?
faq.answer: During the Third War, Archmage Arugal summoned Worgen with research by the late Dalaran wizard Ur. He hoped they would strengthen the Kirin Tor against the Scourge, but the beasts turned on everyone.

faq.q: How does someone become a worgen?
aliases: can you turn into a worgen
faq.answer: Worgen spread a supernatural affliction. A bite or scratch from an active Worgen infects humanoids, and victims eventually succumb to feral urges and become wolf-beasts unless held back by potent discipline or specialized sorcery.

faq.q: What is the Scythe of Elune?
faq.answer: The Scythe of Elune is a powerful night elf relic. It holds deep, volatile dominion over Worgen and can summon and agitate them.

Archmage Arugal was a Kirin Tor archmage of Dalaran. After summoning Worgen to fight the Scourge, he succumbed to madness and came to rule the haunted ruins of Shadowfang Keep with his monstrous children.

faq.q: Why are worgen in Ashenvale and Kalimdor?
faq.answer: Worgen packs now prowl Ashenvale and Felwood, and the Sentinels of Darnassus still seek to learn how they came to Kalimdor. Their search follows the trail of the vanished Sentinel Velinde Starsong and the Scythe of Elune.

angles.text: Worgen show the danger of summoning savage power without the wisdom to control it. Their spread through Kalimdor's forests troubles the Cenarion Circle.
For the kaldorei, Worgen remain a troubling mystery. Sentinels now find the beasts prowling Ashenvale and Felwood.
In Silverpine Forest, the Forsaken battle feral Worgen packs and Arugal's twisted cultists for control of the region south of the Ruins of Lordaeron.
Dalaran's Kirin Tor long debated the research in Ur's mystical treatises. Arugal's catastrophic summoning proved Ur's warnings that these nightmare creatures should never be called forth.
